name: Limit Fix Plan
description: Make the saved provider connection limit a meaningful per-connection parallelism knob by aligning dispatch, request concurrency, and chunk fan-out to the same upper bound.

userStories.title: Count active and queued prompts in dispatch capacity
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want dispatch runtime capacity to subtract both queued and active prompts so claimed backlog reflects the real prompt budget reserved on each provider connection.
acceptanceCriteria: Update `src/server/cron/judgmentsJobs/judgmentDispatchRuntime.ts` so remaining provider capacity uses `pendingPromptCount + activePrompts.length` instead of queued prompts alone.
`enqueueClaimedPrompts(...)` accepts claimed prompts only when the connection still has real headroom after counting both queued and active prompts.
`getProviderQueueCapacity(...)` reports remaining connection headroom rather than only free queue slots.

userStories.title: Launch claimed prompts in bounded parallel per connection
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want per-connection prompt dispatch to launch up to the saved provider limit so raising that limit materially increases local parallelism for normal prompt jobs.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the serial per-connection launch loop in `src/server/cron/judgmentsJobs/judgmentsJobsSendToLLM.ts` with bounded parallel launch per provider connection.
The per-connection launch cap uses the effective provider connection limit for the claimed prompts being processed.
Remove or sharply reduce the current per-prompt launch jitter so available request capacity can fill quickly after claims are made.

userStories.title: Stop new launches on connection failure and requeue only untouched prompts
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want parallel prompt dispatch to track started prompts so connection failures halt new launches without requeueing prompts that already entered their normal retry or recovery path.
acceptanceCriteria: Track which claimed prompts have started launch before invoking LLM processing in `src/server/cron/judgmentsJobs/judgmentsJobsSendToLLM.ts`.
If endpoint availability flips to `skip` or a `ConnectionError` occurs, stop scheduling new prompts for that provider connection.
Requeue only claimed prompts that never started launch, while already-started prompts continue on their existing retry or recovery behavior.

userStories.title: Cap chunked prompt fan-out by the provider limit
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want chunked judging to use the same provider cap so one large prompt cannot consume more request slots than the connection-level upper bound on its own.
acceptanceCriteria: Update `src/agent/judge.ts` so chunk concurrency uses the minimum of `judgeChunkMaxParallel`, `providerMaxInflightRequests` when present, and `chunkCount`.
When no provider cap is saved, chunked judging falls back to the existing configured chunk parallelism behavior instead of becoming serial by accident.
Add or update `src/agent/judge/judgeChunkedMode.test.ts` to cover provider-cap-limited chunk concurrency selection.

userStories.title: Lock in request runtime as the final provider-cap guardrail
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want request runtime coverage to prove provider request concurrency never exceeds local caps even after prompt dispatch becomes more parallel.
acceptanceCriteria: Add or update `src/server/cron/judgmentsJobs/judgmentsRequestRuntime.test.ts` so provider-scoped request caps remain enforced after the dispatch parallelism changes.
Tests cover the case where worker or fallback capacity is lower than the saved provider limit so observed active calls can legitimately plateau below the configured value.
No actual LLM request path added by this work bypasses `withJudgmentRequest(...)` as the authoritative request guardrail.

userStories.title: Clarify backlog and throughput metrics on the job detail page
userStories.description: As a user, I want the job detail page to describe claimed backlog, running prompts, and active LLM calls accurately so higher parallelism is understandable while a job is running.
acceptanceCriteria: Update `src/app/routes/+admin/+jobs/+$id/+index.tsx` only if needed so `Claimed` means reserved local backlog not yet running, `Running Prompts` means prompt executions started locally, and `Active LLM Calls` remains the primary live throughput metric.
The page copy does not imply the configured provider limit is a per-job total when multiple jobs share the same provider connection.
Any copy change preserves the current job-detail layout and data wiring.
